entries.note: Marcus poses a speculative question rather than asserting that a pause will occur. Both “perhaps” and “might” express possibility.

entries.test: Public technical investigations of the Tesla recall and Bing and Bard failures could establish whether all three stemmed from shared limitations of big data and deep learning alone.
entries.note: “Not independent” attributes the failures to a shared technical limitation, rather than claiming direct interaction between the companies.

entries.test: Public architecture documentation and independently verified deployment results could show whether AI built from big data and deep learning alone works in real-world applications.
entries.note: This is a categorical technical claim; demonstrated real-world counterexamples could refute it.

entries.test: Public evaluations and failure analyses could establish whether contemporary deep-learning systems lacked the edge-case robustness and reasoning needed for their intended real-world uses.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion supplies a practical reference point: the real-world failures of Tesla, Bing, and Bard.
This recommends a change in research approach.

entries.test: Public promotional claims about contemporary AI, compared with independently documented capabilities and failures, could establish whether its capabilities were exaggerated.
entries.note: The plain reading of “oversold” is that representations of AI capabilities exceeded demonstrated performance.
